# Cache Policies

## Tier Rationale

**Essential — TLS-only connections and identity-based access.**
Azure Cache for Redis frequently holds session tokens, computed query results, and other high-value transient data. The baseline disables non-SSL ports (TLS 1.2+ only), requires Microsoft Entra ID authentication instead of access keys, and enforces secure-connections-only on every client. These controls map to ISO 27001 A.8.24 (cryptography in transit), A.5.15 (access control), and CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark recommendations for in-memory data stores. Without them an attacker who reaches the network path can downgrade to plaintext or replay an exfiltrated access key.

**Professional — Public network access closed.**
At this tier the cache is no longer addressable from the public internet by default. Operations must maintain the allowed-network configuration and respond when an application legitimately needs a new path in. This addresses NIS2 Article 21(2)(d) supply-chain security and the CIS Benchmark guidance on minimizing exposure of session-bearing data services.

**Enterprise — Private link, customer-managed keys for Enterprise tier.**
Enterprise customers route the cache exclusively through Private Link / Private Endpoints with Private DNS zones, so there is no public DNS resolution and no public route. Redis Enterprise SKUs additionally encrypt on-disk data with customer-managed keys held in Key Vault, providing the full key-lifecycle control (rotation, revocation, audit) that regulators expect. This combination maps to ISO 27001 A.10/A.8.24 (cryptography), NIS2 Article 21(2)(h) on cryptography and key management, and the data-sovereignty requirements common in financial and healthcare workloads.
